recipes.introduction: The large value is the current result or entry. The caption names what it represents, such as Diagonal, Throat radius or Riser height.

sections.text: Feet/inch/fraction forms are lengths. Square units are area; cubic units are volume. A degree sign is an angle. DMS gives degrees.minutes.seconds. A plain number may be a ratio, count or arithmetic result; read the caption with it.
sections.title: Units belong to the value

sections.text: Inputs are values you assigned to the setup. Results are calculated from those inputs. A result cycle may also show entered measurements; read the caption to identify the displayed value.
sections.title: Stored and calculated values

sections.text: For modes with several results, press = to advance through the named outputs and return to the beginning. The worked guides list those outputs in order. Starting another function or editing a value can end the cycle.
sections.title: Read every output in a cycle

sections.text: 2nd puts the second functions on the buttons for your next key press. Parenthesis depth tracks open groups. A stair caution compares calculated values with saved targets; use the actual riser/tread results to assess your layout.
sections.title: Modifiers and cautions

sections.text: Most displayed fractions and decimals are rounded while arithmetic keeps the underlying value. Stairs round step dimensions before downstream calculations. If your result differs from an example, first compare its shown settings and inputs.
